rawCandidates.selectionReason: Premium object-led shop hero for handmade ceramics without needing a generic store grid first.
Lifestyle commerce hero plus staff-picks rhythm fits artisan product storytelling.
Simple store homepage helps calibrate the minimum viable purchase path.
Category carousel maps directly to mugs, planters, dinnerware, and gift-order browsing.
Handmade product grid shows buyer information needs, but needs strong banned-use controls.
Shop-by-color rail fits glaze/color browsing for ceramics.
Editorial homewares blocks are useful for curated studio-market and set-order explanation.
Arrival-led shop structure can become a latest-drop ceramics section.
Product-card layout has strong photo, description, price, and learn-more balance.
Buy-now plus learn-more card state is useful for ready-to-ship versus set-enquiry split.
Object-still-life strip suggests a refined non-stock material visual system.
Retail category rail and shopping-help prompts are useful as a scale reference.
Inventory grouping is useful as an internal anti-reference and search/filter warning.
Saved home-items grid shows B2B price/minimum/favorite complexity to avoid or simplify.
Large category tiles help structure ready-to-ship, dinnerware sets, gifts, and studio-market paths.
Dense commerce grid is a useful anti-reference for a small artisan storefront.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Make the first decision a product purchase or set enquiry, not a generic brand admiration moment.
Use one large object-led hero with a direct shop or latest-drop CTA before category browsing.
Use restrained editorial type that makes handmade products feel considered without fake luxury claims.
Let one approved ceramic still life carry the first viewport if real product media exists.

bannedUses: Do not copy HODINKEE watch imagery, vintage claims, resale categories, insurance links, or luxury scarcity language.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Expose mugs, planters, dinnerware, gifts, and studio market as shopper paths before deep inventory.
Use category copy that explains buying intent: ready-to-ship, small set enquiry, or in-person market visit.
Carousel categories must become scrollable, thumb-friendly rows on mobile.
Use Portland studio-market language, local pickup/visit labels, and US currency only when source-backed.

bannedUses: Do not copy wholesale marketplace language, brand-count claims, trade-show discounts, product photos, or Faire account/cart affordances.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Product cards need image, product name, price/availability if verified, and a clear add/view action.
Cards need sold-out, made-to-order, enquiry-only, selected, hover, focus, and loading states.
Small dinnerware sets should route to a short enquiry form instead of a fake add-to-cart flow.
Only show ratings, bestseller badges, discounts, order urgency, or reviews when Moss & Kiln provides proof.

bannedUses: Do not copy Etsy seller badges, ratings, discounts, scarcity text, shipping claims, ad labels, or marketplace basket controls.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Glaze/color browsing can become a real commerce filter if the palette is restrained and product-backed.
Use clay, glaze, shelf, and paper-like surfaces rather than generic ecommerce gray cards.
Let product silhouettes and simple pill CTAs carry softness; avoid rounded-card overload.
Color/category chips should filter products or scroll to real collections, not act as decorative tags.

bannedUses: Do not copy IKEA photography, product names, shop-by-color labels, room-set scale, or mass-retail tone.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Write like a clear studio operator: material, use case, care, pickup/order path, and availability.
Give product editorial blocks generous whitespace so handmade detail feels inspectable.
Depth should come from photography, overlap, and section rhythm rather than heavy shadows.
If photos are thin, use glaze swatches, kiln marks, maker notes, or line drawings as truthful support.

bannedUses: Do not copy IKEA sustainability claims, affordability framing, trend language, or furniture/home-room copy.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Ready-to-ship pieces should use buy/view CTAs while set orders use enquire CTAs.
Product-card CTAs, price text, image alt text, and filters need keyboard and screen-reader labels.
Use optimized product images and avoid heavy galleries until the core inventory path is fast.
Tokenize product-card width, image ratio, CTA height, gap, focus ring, and clay/glaze colors.

bannedUses: Do not copy Hims medical copy, subscription notes, provider claims, ingredient claims, or regulated disclaimers.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Build a ceramics still-life strip from approved products, clay tools, glaze swatches, or truthful abstract material references.
If motion is used, limit it to subtle product rail reveal, add-to-cart feedback, or market-date reveal.
Use simple utility icons only for pickup, shipping, set enquiry, care, and market visit.
Visible collection names and product availability should map to agent-readable product facts and local market info.

bannedUses: Do not copy Maze SaaS positioning, research/product-decision claims, colored 3D props, or customer-insight proof.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Split shopper paths into buy a piece, enquire about a set, buy a gift, or visit the market.
Block claims about handmade volume, lead times, kiln process, sustainability, or market dates unless source-backed.
Keep currency, pickup, shipping, and market-visit labels local and explicit.
Large category tiles should stack cleanly and keep the primary purchase/enquiry path visible on mobile.

bannedUses: Do not copy meal-kit categories, shipping thresholds, food photography, subscription logic, or pantry-market claims.

antiReferences.rejectionReason: Internal inventory grid language would make a public ceramics shop feel like an admin tool.
Dense marketplace grid, QR/app footer, ratings, discounts, and broad product mix are wrong for a small artisan storefront.
Dark fintech hero, mega-menu complexity, and trading CTAs create the wrong trust model and tone.
SaaS proof screenshots, AI banner, and enterprise CTAs do not translate to a product-led ceramics shop.

remixDirection.summary: A product-led ceramics storefront with an object-led hero, glaze/category browsing, clear ready-to-ship versus set-enquiry paths, and truthful studio-market/local pickup context.
selectedMoves: HODINKEE object-led hero discipline, rebuilt around approved ceramics media and a purchase CTA.
Faire category-carousel logic for mugs, planters, dinnerware, gifts, and studio market browsing.
Etsy product-card information density, stripped of marketplace badges, fake ratings, and scarcity.
IKEA shop-by-color rail adapted into glaze/color collection filtering.
Hims buy-now/learn-more product-card state adapted to buy ready-to-ship or enquire about a set.
explicitRejects: No invented product photos, prices, stock counts, discounts, ratings, reviews, maker claims, sustainability claims, or market dates.
No marketplace clutter, admin inventory UI, SaaS proof screenshots, crypto/finance tone, or exact layout copy.
No exact layout copy from any shortlisted Mobbin screen.
